headline: High risk of cascading error and medium prompt-injection/data-leakage exposure when pdf.js outputs feed Plane workflows; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty is escalated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js can run browsers and processes PDF files, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. A plausible bridge exists if pdf.js output is copied into Plane or shared via files, letting attacker-controlled PDF content influence downstream interpretation. No direct shared channel is documented, so I escalate from low to medium under uncertainty.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is pasted or uploaded into Plane without sanitization
IF a PDF contains instruction-like text that Plane users treat as authoritative
mitigations: Use a manual review step before importing PDF-derived text into Plane
Strip active content and hidden text from PDFs before processing
Label imported PDF content as untrusted in Plane
Restrict Plane uploads to vetted documents only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from pdf.js to Plane

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and Plane handles files, notes, hyperlinks, and uploads. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive PDF contents can flow into Plane outputs. pdf.js has no network egress, which limits exfiltration, but Plane has broad egress and file uploads, so the shared-data pathway is still plausible and not default-safe.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain sensitive or regulated data
IF pdf.js outputs are transferred into Plane via upload, copy-paste, or shared storage
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in any shared workspace
Disable or limit Plane uploads for sensitive projects
Redact PDFs before importing them into Plane
Keep pdf.js and Plane on separate storage locations
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js does not request filesystem write or network egress, while Plane also shows no filesystem write capability but does have broad network egress. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because both support multiple instances and Plane can handle files, but the profiles do not show a shared mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource through an unlisted integration
IF Plane is configured to write into a shared directory outside the documented profile
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid shared mutable folders or mounts
Run only one writer for any external resource
Document any integration points before enabling them
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can extract or render PDF content, and Plane can store notes, issues, and hyperlinks. If pdf.js output is forwarded into Plane without verification, Plane may preserve or act on incorrect text. The profiles do not prove automatic chaining, so this is medium rather than high, but the pathway is plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF pdf.js-derived text is imported into Plane as a task, note, or issue
IF Plane users rely on that imported content without independent verification
mitigations: Verify extracted PDF text against the source document
Require human review before creating Plane tasks from PDF output
Mark imported content as draft or untrusted
Limit automation from pdf.js into Plane to summaries only
requires-engineering: add validation checks before task creation

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no PHI, residency, or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance surface is that pdf.js processes PDF documents while Plane stores files and notes, so a compliance issue would arise only if regulated documents are moved between them. The other agent is cited because the risk depends on the pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated documents are uploaded into Plane after being processed by pdf.js
IF the operator requires residency or retention controls not documented in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of Plane unless policy is confirmed
Review retention settings before uploading documents
Use separate handling for regulated and non-regulated files
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls
